findings.content: Offer requires: (1) definite terms, (2) intention to be bound, (3) communication. E1 provides definite terms; E3 demonstrates intention.
Acceptance by performance requires: (1) knowledge of offer, (2) performance of specified act. E2 shows performance; E1 defines act.
Intention to create legal relations required. £1000 deposit (E3) is objective manifestation of intent, satisfying this necessary condition.
Unilateral offer requires no notification; performance IS acceptance. Offer terms (E1) specify performance as acceptance mode.
Advertisement's specific terms (reward amount, usage instructions, deposit) indicate legal offer, not puffery. This assumption is necessary for contract formation.
Mrs. Carlill's usage (E2) constitutes exact performance per printed directions. Assumption: directions were followed exactly.
£1000 deposit at Alliance Bank (E3) is objective manifestation of intent, satisfying this necessary condition.
Advertisement could be interpreted as invitation to treat, but specificity and deposit rebut this.
Specific terms (reward amount, usage frequency, duration) indicate legal offer, not puffery.
Deposit at Alliance Bank (not company's own bank) is objectively verifiable act of commitment.
Deposit at Alliance Bank (not company's own bank) is objectively verifiable act of commitment.

summary: First-principles analysis confirms all four requirements satisfied: offer with definite terms (R1), acceptance by performance (R2), intention to create legal relations (R3), and no notification required for unilateral offer (R4). Contract formed upon performance.
uncertainties: Whether Mrs. Carlill's performance was exactly per printed directions
Whether modern courts would extend this to digital offers
